report:
Conclusion
- The evidence supports a real, interpretable difference: Model B (minus A) pushes probability mass toward professional/academic and culinary/restaurant vocabulary (and some technical/industrial terms). In other words, B is biased toward tokens like dissertation/doctoral/undergraduate/professional/technical and restaurant/cooking/Chef/baking/culinary.

Why I conclude this
- Token-level evidence: Across the highest-norm residual cells, the logit-lens top tokens repeatedly include "dissertation", "doctoral", "undergraduate", "professional", "technical", "molecular", "Innovation/innovative", and a dense cluster of culinary/restaurant words ("restaurant", "Restaurant", "cooking", "Cooking", "culinary", "Chef", "kitchen", "baking", "Cook", "Cake", "hot", "hottest", "delectable", "exquisite"). Petrochemical/polyurethane and macroeconomic/billionaire also appear, suggesting some technical/industrial and high-status lexical shifts as well.
- Localization in the network: the L2-norm differences concentrate in middle-to-late layers (roughly layers 10–25) and particularly at early token positions (pos1 in many layers shows especially large values). That pattern indicates the change acts early in generation and is implemented by later processing stages, consistent with a shift in preferred lexical choices rather than (only) low-level formatting.
- Consistency across many high-norm cells: the same semantic clusters (academic/professional and culinary) recur across many different (layer,position) cells, making it unlikely to be a random fluctuation.

Caveats / limits
- There are at least two semantic clusters (academic/professional and culinary/restaurant) rather than a single narrowly defined domain, so I cannot confidently name one single precise objective (e.g., "restaurant-review specialist" vs "resume/academic style"). The evidence supports a broader shift toward professional/technical and food/restaurant vocabulary.
- Patchscope continuations were not provided here, so the conclusion rests mainly on logit-lens projections and the layer/position localization.

If you want, I can: (a) inspect lower-ranked logit-lens tokens or more cells to see whether one cluster dominates; (b) run patchscope continuations (or show them) to confirm how the difference manifests in actual text.
